issues.cell: Part L law 2 (c) (adj l. 506-521: the generation paragraph's 'F-REDERIVE's for a run water re-traces', the epoch and hand paragraphs) x *the tiers* (adj l. 339-344; J148) x law 2 (a) (adj l. 483-491); W1 at an epoch (a run an epoch's moved river or carve re-traces); E-D12, E-S12, E-V6-15, R7-02's (G3), bent-group and fixed-place sentences, veto 22's record; Part P pass 5's re-check (adj l. 3320) of PRB7B-08
issues.claim: An epoch shiftCourse, avulsion or digCanal (or a hand carve) whose re-traced run - the run between the nearest towers the water leaves unaffected (base l. 8302-8304, 10927, 11003-11005) - has no lawful shape at a standing raised way: law 2 (c)'s epoch and hand paragraphs make the water op wait or refuse it, yet the same law names 'F-REDERIVE's for a run water re-traces' among the generation, regeneration and village-derivation rungs (where no water op re-traces a run), with words ('search band widened ... beyond the stage's boundary ... else the stage left unwalled') that have no reading for a re-traced run. E-D12 (written as given), E-S12's T110-2 (4) and R7-02's sentences run the rung on the epoch and hand paths: 'the run widened once to the next unaffected tower on each side and re-traced'. Widening makes the two former end towers - standing, untouched by the water - interior: §7.3 (b) 3 removes the old run and S7 builds towers at the re-traced run's vertices and a gate at each crossing (base l. 11015-11020, 11058-11060, 10927), so standing towers, gates and posterns are re-laid for the meeting - the move J148 withdrew (law 2 (a) plans round every Tier-1 thing; (b) moves Tier-3 things only). Pass 5 withdrew what only a moved Tier-1 thing needed but kept 'PRB7B-08's rung' standing (adj l. 3320): that closure fails. Two builds differ on the ring's towers and gates, the river's course and walls.waited; both pass every bar (PRB7F-TIM-03).
issues.required_change: Part L law 2 (c), adj l. 510: 'that stage's raised-way rung runs alone (F-WALL's; F-V-RAISED at a village; F-REDERIVE's for a run water re-traces):' -> 'that stage's raised-way rung runs alone (F-WALL's; F-V-RAISED at a village):'; adj l. 517-519: 'a water op (`shiftCourse`, an avulsion, `digCanal`) being checked on its new water before the water is inserted and waiting likewise;' -> 'a water op (`shiftCourse`, an avulsion, `digCanal`) being checked on its new water before the water is inserted and waiting likewise - its re-traced run laid by (a) within the run its own law re-traces, between the nearest towers the new water leaves unaffected, and never widened past them (J148: no standing tower, gate or postern re-laid for a meeting); by hand, a carve or a moved river whose re-traced run has no lawful shape within that run refused as above;'. Correction 1 (adj l. 579-584), after 'or that drops, refuses or waits a newer structure only because one stands in its way,' add 'or that widens a run a water op re-traces past the nearest towers the water leaves unaffected (F-REDERIVE's raised-way rung: E-D12, E-S12, E-V6-15, R7-02's (G3), bent-group and fixed-place sentences, veto 22's record),'. Part P's *J148 applied* 'Withdrawn with the moves' adds 'F-REDERIVE's raised-way rung's widening of the run to the next unaffected tower on each side (PRB7B-08), which re-laid standing towers, gates and posterns for a meeting'; the re-check (adj l. 3320) reads 'PRB7-16 and PRB7B-09's rungs stand with law 2 (c)'s reach; PRB7B-08's stands but for its widened run (J148)'. Consequences: E-D12's ladder -> '**A wall run with no lawful shape at a raised way** (§2.7's laws, law 2 (c); J148: the run never widened past the towers the water leaves unaffected) -> by hand, `refuse.raised.meeting` (§7.1); at an epoch, the water op that would re-trace it (`shiftCourse`, an avulsion, `digCanal`) not made that epoch, waiting (`walls.waited`, V06 §2.10), the river, the run and the raised way unchanged - never a run across water without its water gate (§5.3)'; E-S12's '- the re-traced run widened once to the next towers, its water gate clear of the zone, and, on a second run where no clear point lies within the widened run,' -> '- its water gate placed along the river clear of the zone within the re-traced run, and, on a second run where no clear point lies within that run,'; E-V6-15's 'whose re-traced run F-REDERIVE's raised-way rung finds no lawful shape for' -> 'whose re-traced run has no lawful shape within the run its own law re-traces (§2.7's laws, law 2 (c))'.

issues.cell: Part L law 1 (2)'s merged ('no gate (no way passes it)', adj l. 401-407) x law 1 (5) ('but under an aqueduct whose every span over it clears its top', adj l. 416-417) x law 1 (6); *J149 applied* (adj l. 3162-3164); W1·C1 at an epoch (V06 §3.19's founding), W14 at a village epoch (V07 §3.11's REPLACEMENT), a re-section raising a wall's top
issues.claim: A postern or a gate with no gatehouse whose own top (Gate.heights, base l. 2275, 1316) lies below the wall's top there (base l. 2262), under an aqueduct span whose soffit lies between the two. (A) Law 1 as written: law 1 (5) asks only that every span over the gate clear its own top - it does - so the gate stands; law 1 (2) reads the crossing merged (the span does not clear the wall's top): the band built round the arch at the gate's passage. The REPLACEMENT ('rebuilt on the palisade's trace ... its full stretches taking the stone section ... gates kept', V07 l. 2288-2291) applies beneath an arch that cleared palisade and gate; V06 §3.19's founded aqueduct may cross at the postern. (B) Law 1 (2)'s 'no gate (no way passes it)' read as a condition, with J149's program reading ('a merge never falls on a gate's passage or in a tower - there the aqueduct bends along its course to plain wall, else gives way', PROGRESS l. 208) and Part P's statement that law 1 (5) 'already give[s]' that exclusion (adj l. 3162-3164): unlawful - the aqueduct bends else raised.waited, the REPLACEMENT waits (the kept gate cannot move, Tier 1). Part P's claim holds only for a gate taller than the wall; for a postern or a passage gate it fails. Two builds lay different aqueduct courses at a CITY epoch, and one rebuilds a village palisade in stone while the other never does; §5.3's row passes each by its own reading.
issues.required_change: Part L law 1 (5) (adj l. 416-417): 'no gate's, postern's or tower's footprint lies in a strip, under a standing span or a fallen one, but under an aqueduct whose every span over it clears its top, never on a support's ring (law 1 (2)'s over; J149);' -> 'no gate's, postern's or tower's footprint lies in a strip, under a standing span or a fallen one, but under an aqueduct whose every span over it clears both its own top and the top of the wall it stands in there - the crossing there law 1 (2)'s over -, never on a support's ring and never in a crossing law 1 (2) reads merged (J149: a merge never on a gate's passage or in a tower);'. Law 1 (2) (adj l. 406): '- no gate (no way passes it), each keeping its own condition (item 114) -' -> '- the merged arch no gate (no way passes it) and no gate, postern or tower standing in it (law 1 (5)), each keeping its own condition (item 114) -'. *J149 applied* (adj l. 3162-3164): 'and two exclusions law 1 (5) and (10) already give (no merge on a gate's passage or in a tower; ...)' -> 'and two exclusions law 1 (5) and (10) give (no merge on a gate's passage or in a tower, law 1 (5) reading the wall's top as well as the gate's; ...)'. Consequence: R7-02's W14 cell (adj l. 1226) and E-V7-6 - 'the REPLACEMENT waiting where a standing gate's stone footprint would meet a strip' - add 'or where its new top would rise past the soffit of an aqueduct's arch over a kept gate (§2.7's laws, law 1 (5))'.

issues.cell: *The tiers* (adj l. 339-344: Tier 1 'is never moved by a meeting'; J148) x law 1 (adj l. 398-437; (10) holds only a held thing) x the check (adj l. 558-572) x E-D13 (adj l. 2121-2135) x T110-4 (E-S13, adj l. 1812-1833); W1 at an epoch, W10, W14, V06 §3.19's founding
issues.claim: J148 is an owner rule about every meeting's result - a gate, postern, tower or fixed place standing when a commit begins stands where it stood when it ends, unless the commit's own op names it or removes it by its own law - but Part L states it only as law 2's order of resolution (*the tiers*, law 2 (a)-(c), correction 1), never in law 1. Law 1 (10) and the check compare placement fields of held things only; T110-4 asserts the placement of locked structures only; law 1 (5) and (6) are met by a moved gate that lands clear of every strip and zone. So a build that keeps law 2 (b)'s withdrawn moves (adj l. 3096-3098) or F-REDERIVE's widened run (PRB7F-TIM-01) leaves law 1 (1)-(10) true at every commit's end and passes every bar - the edge an owner rule defines with no bar that runs it (R7-01's grading, adj l. 252-254), the very question pass 5's verdict left open ('whether any bar observes a meeting that moves an unheld Tier-1 thing (law 1 (10) sees it only for a held one)', adj l. 3339-3342).
issues.required_change: Part L law 1, after (10) (adj l. 437), add: '11. no gate, postern, tower or fixed place standing when a commit begins is moved, re-laid or removed by a meeting: each stands at the commit's end in the place its record held as the event began (its junction or vertex, its `banks`, its anchor, with its footprint there), save one the event names as its own target or that the event's own law moves, re-lays or removes whatever it meets - a gate the user places, slides or deletes; a run deleted, buried, absorbed and dismantled, or converted by `wallToWay` or `gateToJunction`; the run a water op re-traces between the nearest towers the new water leaves unaffected; a castle re-sited whole; a regeneration's stage laying it again (*Newer*) - (J148).' The check (adj l. 563-567), after '(10) by each held structure ... unless the event names it as its own target (...)' add '; (11) by each gate, postern, tower and fixed place of every wall-like structure the commit touched against its record as the event began, the fields of its place unchanged but as (11) excepts'. Consequences: E-D13's third cell adds 'each gate, postern, tower and fixed place of a touched wall-like structure against its record as the event began (§2.7's laws, law 1 (11))'; E-S13's T110-4 adds, after 'every locked structure's placement, and every shape-locked one's shape, unchanged by every op that does not name it': '; no gate, postern, tower or fixed place moved, re-laid or removed for a meeting, locked or not (§2.7's laws, law 1 (11); J148)'.

issues.cell: J149 (law 1 (2), (5), (7)) x the lens's live bars: T-V6-47 (V06 l. 4170), T-V7-48 (V07 l. 3683), T110-2 (1) (base l. 18540-18546, taken by T-V6-73), R7-02's W6·C2 (adj l. 1218); E-V6-8, E-V7-1, E-S1 (append only); Part H's one rule (adj l. 1590-1599); the scope, V06 and V07 sweeps (adj l. 1848-1849, 2404, 2472)
issues.claim: Correction 7 reads R7-02's examples and Part H's one rule reads 'every END line's quoted new text and every FIX' by J149, but the lens's live bars keep the old aqueduct crossing and their END lines only append after them, while each unit's sweep says nothing else changes. On a correct build each fails: T-V6-47's H-AQUA circuit and contraction ('the trace crossing it under a span, no support ... in its band but a support's edge, a run ... capped at the lowest soffit there, ... no gate or tower in the under-deck strip'; bar '0 gates or towers in an under-deck strip; 0 wall runs above a standing span's soffit ...; 0 trace lines across ... an aqueduct's standing support'); T-V7-48 ('its line bent to cross the declared aqueduct under a span'; '0 gates in an under-deck strip'; '0 palisade runs above a standing span's soffit'; 'a hand aqueduct ... its supports off the band, a span over it'); T110-2 (1) ('its supports off the band ...', 'the run beneath at the lower of its own top and the soffit', 'S7's towers clear of its under-deck strip, one its spacing placed there moved along the trace'); R7-02's W6·C2 ('no gate stands in an under-deck strip, so none it opens lies under a deck' - a gate under an aqueduct's clearing arch now does).
issues.required_change: END lines citing §2.7's laws. V06 (new E-V6-8 (4)): T-V6-47's 'the trace crossing it under a span, no support, ramp, stair or foot in its band but a support's edge, a run beneath each standing span and across a support bearing one capped at the lowest soffit there' -> 'the trace crossing its deck line once, over or merged by the aqueduct's level (§2.7's laws, law 1 (2)), no ramp, stair or foot in its band, the run at its own top beneath the aqueduct (law 1 (7))'; 'no gate or tower in the under-deck strip' -> 'no gate or tower in the under-deck strip but under an arch that clears it and the wall (law 1 (5))'; the bar's '0 gates or towers in an under-deck strip; 0 wall runs above a standing span's soffit, at a span or at a support bearing it; 0 trace lines across a ramp, stair, foot or an aqueduct's standing support' -> '0 gates or towers in an under-deck strip but under an aqueduct's arch that clears them and the wall; 0 wall runs above a standing road-deck span's soffit, at a span or at a support bearing it; 0 trace lines across a ramp, stair or foot; each crossing of an aqueduct's deck line over or merged (law 1 (2))'. V07 (new E-V7-8): T-V7-48's 'its line bent to cross the declared aqueduct under a span and' -> 'its line crossing the declared aqueduct's deck line once, over or merged (§2.7's laws, law 1 (2)), and'; '0 gates in an under-deck strip' -> '0 gates in an under-deck strip but under an aqueduct's arch that clears them and the palisade (law 1 (5))'; '0 palisade runs above a standing span's soffit' -> '0 palisade runs above a standing road-deck span's soffit (law 1 (7))'; '- its supports off the band, a span over it' -> '- over the palisade or merged into it (law 1 (2))'. Scope (new E-S17): T110-2 (1)'s 'its supports off the band and out of the moat's water' -> 'its supports out of the moat's water, the ring crossed over or merged by its level (§2.7's laws, law 1 (2))'; 'the run beneath at the lower of its own top and the soffit' -> 'the run at its own top (law 1 (7))'; 'S7's towers clear of its under-deck strip, one its spacing placed there moved along the trace' -> 'S7's towers clear of its under-deck strip but under an arch that clears them and the wall, one its spacing placed elsewhere in it moved along the trace (law 1 (5); law 2 (a))'. R7-02's W6·C2: '*unchanged meeting*: no gate stands in an under-deck strip, so none it opens lies under a deck' -> '*unchanged meeting*: a gate it opens under an aqueduct's arch that clears it becomes a junction there, its square laid as at any gate and read across the span's strip (§2.7's laws, law 1 (5), (8)); none stands under a road deck'.
